extracted.subtask_description: Rules, conduct, and scene-setting for a boys' boat-club story aimed at young readers; includes the in-story constitution, meeting procedure, uniforms, and behavioral expectations that shape plot and character actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article I — Name of the association
rubrics_metrics.description: This association shall be called the Zephyr Boat Club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of the name was voted on at the first meeting (unanimous vote for 'Zephyr Hall'); names and naming may be proposed, seconded, debated briefly, and formally recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article II — Objects of the association
rubrics_metrics.description: The objects of the association shall be the instruction and amusement of the members, and the acquiring of good morals, good manners, and good habits in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States the club's purpose as both recreational and moral/educational — sets tone for behavioral expectations and justification for disciplinary provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article III — Officers of the club
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers of the club shall consist of a coxswain, as president, and a clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines minimum officer roles; the coxswain presides and the clerk records business. Further duties and terms given in Articles IV and V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article IV — Duty and term of coxswain
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be the duty of the coxswain to command the boat, to preside at the meetings of the club, and to exercise a general supervision over its affairs. He shall hold his office for two weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coxswain must lead in both boating and meetings, enforce discipline, and carry responsibility for club conduct while in office for a fixed short term (two weeks). Example: Frank acting as coxswain, making orders, and reporting offences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article V — Duty and term of clerk
rubrics_metrics.description: The clerk shall keep a record of the meetings, and of all business pertaining to the club, and shall hold his office for four weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes record-keeping and continuity (clerk term longer than coxswain). Practical steps: ballots, counting votes, transferring constitution to record book and signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article VI — Member conduct prohibitions and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: No member of this club shall use profane language at any time. No member shall neglect his school, or his duties at home. No member shall use vulgar or indecent language. No member shall provoke a quarrel with another person, but shall do all he can to prevent fighting and unkindly feelings one towards another. No member shall use tobacco, or ardent spirits as a beverage, in any form. All members shall obey the coxswain while in the boat. Any member offending against either of the requirements of this article shall be liable to suspension, and if incorrigible, to expulsion from the club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed behavioral code covering language, school/home duties, smoking/drinking, provocation/peacemaking, and obedience in-boat. Violations trigger discretionary discipline (suspension/expulsion) and are treated seriously; example incidents are referred to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article VII — Director and reporting of violations
rubrics_metrics.description: In order the more perfectly to carry out the beneficent and reformatory purposes of the founder of the club, to whose bounty we are indebted for the opportunities of instruction and amusement the association affords us, we appoint him our Director. All violations of Article VI., and all violations of the spirit of our organization set forth in Article II., whether in word or in deed, shall be reported to our Director, and the delinquent shall be subject to such penalty as he shall determine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates a founder/Director with discretionary authority over penalties and the reformatory purpose of the club; reporting mechanism centralizes discipline with the Director rather than collective vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article VIII — Hall and library hours
rubrics_metrics.description: The hall and library shall be open every Wednesday and Saturday afternoon, at such other times as the Director or coxswain may order, and every evening except Sunday till nine o'clock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies access times and the authoritative power of Director/coxswain to adjust hours; demonstrates structured use of club facilities for instruction and amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article IX — Amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: This constitution may be altered or amended by a vote of two-thirds of the members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a supermajority rule for constitutional changes — stability with a democratic amendment pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary procedure for meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings are conducted with formal parliamentary usage: 'Order!' to call to order; motions must be made and seconded; the chair states the question and opens for debate; members may rise to obtain the floor; the chair can put the question ('Question!'); votes may be taken by show of hands; committees may be appointed to collect and count ballots; the clerk records votes and minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The club used Cushing's 'Manual' as instruction; members had observed town meetings to learn procedure. Examples in the text include making and withdrawing motions, appointing committees of three to count votes, and recording results in the record book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform specification and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: White sailors' trousers, a blue jacket, and a white shirt trimmed with blue. The hat will be a tarpaulin, with 'Zephyr' in gilt letters on the front.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniforms were procured from a tailor, numbered and stored in closets, and worn for public presentation; uniforms strengthen group identity and public reception (people gathered to watch them row).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rowing discipline and drill commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of naval/boat commands and precise drill: 'Push off', 'Up oars', 'Let fall', 'Give way together', 'Shove off', 'Way enough', 'Stern all', 'Back her steady', 'Lay on your oars'. Discipline and synchronized stroke were emphasized and trained by Uncle Ben.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on practice and precision: 'the manoeuvre was executed with admirable precision'; good command of boating technique both for safety and to impress the public. Obedience to coxswain orders during rowing is mandatory (Article VI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership conduct for the coxswain
rubrics_metrics.description: Coxswain must command the boat, preside at meetings, exercise general supervision, hold office for two weeks, be decisive in emergencies, enforce discipline, but not be tyrannical — yield to majority when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Frank shows firmness (orders to avoid provoking the Bunkers, lands those who misbehave), restraint (not tyrannical), readiness to take responsibility (planning to report offences), and situational bravery (using the boat to protect Tony).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and operational rules for outings
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical safety guidance: don't get aground on the rocks at the north shore, if you go down the river don't go too near the dam, obey the coxswain while in the boat, be careful where you land the boat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captain Sedley warns the boys explicitly; Frank demonstrates situational awareness (avoids landing at Rippleton to protect the boat). These rules are framed as duties of the coxswain and club to preserve the club's possessions and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict avoidance, resolution, and reparations
rubrics_metrics.description: Members should not provoke quarrels and should prevent fighting; violations should be reported; penalties include suspension/expulsion; reparations for damage may be paid by members (example: Fred and the club raised money to pay Tim Bunker $1.50 for damaged gunwale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows a preference for restitution and forgiveness where possible ('forgive and forget') but also formal reporting and sanctions via the Director when necessary. Practical handling of disputes may include monetary settlement to avoid escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-keeping and formalization of constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: The constitution was transferred to the record book, and duly signed. The clerk keeps the record of the meetings and all business pertaining to the club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the formal, written record as part of club governance; ballots, counts, and officer elections are recorded. Maintaining a signed constitution and minutes supports accountability and continuity.
